title: SDK auth: unify API key resolution order, normalize headers, and redact secrets in logs/exceptions
author: Ibrahim Khan
description:
Context: As part of the cross-SDK parity audit, Python auth behavior needs to match the agreed standard: deterministic API key discovery, a single header scheme, and security-safe error/logging behavior. This PR focuses on (1) API key resolution order, (2) clearer missing/invalid key errors, and (3) guaranteed redaction of API keys in logging and exception surfaces.

What changed: - API key resolution order is now explicit and tested: 1) per-request override (request options) 2) client constructor argument (api_key=...) 3) environment variables (REDWOOD_API_KEY, then REDWOOD_TOKEN for backward compatibility) 4) fall back to "missing key" error (no implicit keychain/file reads). - Header normalization: SDK sends Authorization: Bearer <key> by default. For backwards compatibility, we still accept REDWOOD_TOKEN env var but do not emit legacy header names. - Error messaging: Missing key raises a RedwoodAuthenticationError with remediation steps and the exact env var names. Invalid/unauthorized responses (401/403) are mapped to RedwoodAuthenticationError with a short, non-leaky message and include request_id when present. - Redaction: API keys are never included in exception messages, __repr__/__str__ of client/config, or debug logs. Added a small redaction helper used by request logging and error wrapping. - Docs/typing: updated docstrings on Client and RequestOptions; added type annotations for auth fields; added a short note in the README snippet used by docs.

Why: Support has recurring tickets where customers set the wrong env var name or accidentally log client config during debugging. We also saw ambiguity across SDKs (some used x-api-key, some used Authorization). This PR moves Python to the standard and meets Security’s redaction requirements.

Test plan: - Unit tests for resolution order and header emission. - Unit tests ensuring exceptions do not contain raw secrets (including partial substrings) and that repr(client) is safe. - Integration-ish tests around mapping 401/403 into RedwoodAuthenticationError and preserving request_id.

Notes / non-goals: - No support for reading keys from files (e.g., ~/.redwood) in v1; Security requested we keep discovery explicit. - This PR does not change server behavior; relies on gateway-provided request-id and auth errors.

Release note: Python SDK now prefers Authorization: Bearer for auth and provides clearer missing/invalid API key errors; secrets are always redacted from logs/exceptions. Existing users relying on REDWOOD_TOKEN will continue to work, but REDWOOD_API_KEY is the recommended env var going forward.
commits: auth: introduce ApiKeyProvider and deterministic resolution order
auth: normalize Authorization header and remove legacy header emission
errors: map 401/403 to RedwoodAuthenticationError with request_id
security: add secret redaction helper + repr safety
tests: auth resolution, header emission, redaction invariants
changed_files: redwood/_client.py (wire ApiKeyProvider into request pipeline; safe logging)
redwood/_auth.py (new: ApiKeyProvider, env var lookup, validation)
conversation: Monica Patel (review): Can we confirm the exact env var names we want to document? Also, do we still accept REDWOOD_TOKEN for people who copied old quickstarts?
Ibrahim Khan (author): Yep. Priority is REDWOOD_API_KEY then REDWOOD_TOKEN (compat only). Error message lists both, but calls out REDWOOD_API_KEY as recommended. I added tests to lock this behavior.

Marcus Lin (review): Please ensure keys cannot leak via repr() or exception chaining. We’ve had incidents where libraries include request headers in raised exceptions. Also avoid logging the full Authorization header even in debug.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Added explicit redaction in request logging and scrubbed any header echo in error wrappers. Also added tests that assert the raw key and common prefixes never appear in str(exc) / repr(client).
Kevin Osei (review): Any chance we read from a local file? Some enterprise customers asked. Security preference is explicit, but want to document rationale.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Not in this PR. I added a note under non-goals and kept discovery to ctor/request/env only. We can revisit with a separate ADR if needed.
Rafael Mendes (review): Minor: include request_id in auth errors if available; it helps support correlate. Also ensure we don’t retry on auth failures (even indirectly).
Ibrahim Khan (author): Added request_id passthrough. Retry policy work is in a separate PR, but I ensured auth errors are classified as non-retryable by default in the error taxonomy module.
Marcus Lin (request changes): One more thing: ensure redaction also covers partial leaks (e.g., first 8 chars). Some libraries do this to be ‘helpful’.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Good catch. Updated helper to replace any detected token-like substrings and removed any partial token rendering. Added a regression test that fails if first/last segments show up.
Marcus Lin (approve): Looks good after the redaction updates. Approved.
Monica Patel (approve): Approved. Let’s make sure release notes mention the recommended env var name and that REDWOOD_TOKEN is deprecated-but-supported.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-02-03 by Monica Patel
release_notes: Python SDK auth standardized: deterministic API key resolution (request > client > env), Authorization: Bearer header normalization, clearer missing/invalid key errors, and guaranteed API key redaction in logs/exceptions. REDWOOD_TOKEN remains supported for compatibility; REDWOOD_API_KEY is recommended.
